bounded_lqr_umax_high.description: Context-only bounded LQR OCP with u_max=10^4: timing for solving n_batch=128 problems with adjoint sensitivities. N=20, nx=8, nu=4, n_theta=248. From Table 1 of the paper. All metric coefficients are zero because wall-clock metrics are hardware-dependent in this gym.

solve_and_sens_time_ms.description: Context-only wall-clock total solve-plus-adjoint-sensitivity latency for the 128 bounded-LQR problems. It is not scored because hardware varies across ResearchGym runs.

per_problem_solve_and_sens_ms.description: Context-only wall-clock latency normalized by the 128-problem batch size. It is not scored because no machine-independent LQR proxy is exposed in the frozen artifact.

speedup_vs_mpc_pytorch.description: Paper-reported contextual speedup against mpc.pytorch; retained for reference validation but not used for split scoring because the evaluator does not compute it.

speedup_vs_cvxpygen.description: Paper-reported contextual speedup against cvxpygen/OSQP; retained for reference validation but not used for split scoring because the evaluator does not compute it.

bounded_lqr_umax_low.description: Context-only bounded LQR OCP with u_max=1.0: timing for solving n_batch=128 problems with adjoint sensitivities. N=20, nx=8, nu=4, n_theta=248. From Table 1 of the paper. Note: mpc.pytorch fails to converge consistently in this setting. All metric coefficients are zero because wall-clock metrics are hardware-dependent in this gym.

solve_and_sens_time_ms.description: Context-only wall-clock total solve-plus-adjoint-sensitivity latency for the 128 tight-bound LQR problems. It is not scored because hardware varies across ResearchGym runs.

per_problem_solve_and_sens_ms.description: Context-only wall-clock latency normalized by the 128-problem batch size. It is not scored because no machine-independent LQR proxy is exposed in the frozen artifact.

tight_to_loose_runtime_ratio.description: Context-only tight-bound wall-clock runtime divided by loose-bound runtime. It is retained for diagnostics but not scored.

speedup_vs_mpc_pytorch.description: Paper-reported contextual speedup against mpc.pytorch; retained for reference validation but not used for split scoring because the evaluator does not compute it.

speedup_vs_cvxpygen.description: Paper-reported contextual speedup against cvxpygen/OSQP; retained for reference validation but not used for split scoring because the evaluator does not compute it.

pendulum_sensitivity_accuracy.description: Highly-parametric pendulum OCP: sensitivity accuracy vs finite differences. Cart-pole system, N=50, nx=4, nu=1, n_theta=1. Core claim: acados sensitivities match finite differences, while the Gauss-Newton Hessian approximation gives materially worse sensitivities. The paper presents this comparison graphically in Figure 2 and does not report a numeric Gauss-Newton max-error value; the proposed-method max-error target is the strongest prior reproduced numeric finite-difference error used to anchor the gym.

sensitivity_max_error.description: Visible absolute error between adjoint sensitivity and finite-difference sensitivity at the pendulum reference point.

log10_sensitivity_advantage_vs_gn.description: Held-out log10 ratio of Gauss-Newton sensitivity error to this method's error, rewarding methods that preserve the exact-Hessian advantage over the shortcut baseline.

log10_error_regression_vs_exact.description: Held-out log10 ratio of this method's sensitivity error to the strongest reproduced reference error in the submitted artifact. Values below zero are allowed, so future methods can improve beyond the packaged reproduction.
